skills.name: ascii-music-video
skills.description: Use when someone wants to turn a song (MP3 plus optional lyrics) into a beat-synced ASCII-art music video.
skills.content:
---
name: ascii-music-video
description: >-
  Use when someone wants to turn a song (MP3 plus optional lyrics) into a
  beat-synced ASCII-art music video.
---
Turn a song into a beat-synced ASCII / glyph / dot-art music video. Scenes come from the lyrics, images are generated per scene, and the camera motion follows the beat.

## Inputs
- **MP3 (required).** Suno blocks downloads from share links, so ask the user to export it: open the song on suno.com, use the "..." menu, choose Download, then MP3 Audio, and upload the file here.
- **Lyrics (optional).** A pasted lyrics .txt, or the Suno song link (lyrics only; read them from the public page). Keep Suno's [Verse]/[Hook] tags. Without lyrics, transcribe.
- **Theme / style hint (optional),** e.g. neon noir, cyberpunk, retro arcade. A user's theme always overrides the discovered style.

## Steps
1. **Engine.** `git clone https://github.com/ecoay/ascii-music-video && cd ascii-music-video && bash setup.sh`. If git is missing: `curl -L https://codeload.github.com/ecoay/ascii-music-video/tar.gz/refs/heads/main | tar xz && cd ascii-music-video-main && bash setup.sh`. The first run takes ~2-5 min.
2. **Plan.** `.venv/bin/python plan_scenes.py song.mp3 [--lyrics lyrics.txt] --target 14 --out scenes`. It transcribes, aligns the lyrics and writes ~12-16 scenes. Repeated hooks/choruses reuse one image. Check the match % and the scene list; if scenes are far too long or short, adjust `--target`.
3. **Discover the visual style.** Unless the user named a look, pick ONE visual style for this song from its genre, Suno style tags, tempo, mood and the lyrics' imagery (e.g. moody synthwave gets neon chrome noir; folk gets woodcut ink; trap gets gritty street photo; hymn gets stained-glass light). Write it as one short style line and use it for every scene so the video feels consistent. Tell the user the chosen style with the first preview and offer to change it.
4. **Prompts.** For each entry in `scenes/image_prompts.json`, write a specific image prompt that depicts what the lyric *means* (the metaphor, not the literal words). Use one clear subject and end every prompt with the style line plus: "Dark, high-contrast, single centered subject on pure black background, hard rim light, bold silhouette, no text."
5. **Images.** Generate each with your image tool (16:9) and save it as `scenes/scene_NN.png`, matching the file names.
6. **Preview.** `.venv/bin/python asciimv.py song.mp3 --scenes-json scenes/scenes.json --style auto --skyline --lyrics-overlay -o video.mp4 --stills-only --still <mid-scene times>`.
   - Motion rules: a circular object spins to the tempo; a distant or detailed subject gets a zoom-through into a dark hole that lands on the downbeat; anything else pans/bounces with kick cuts.
   - Style rules: colorful and bright goes to color, dark goes to dots, everything else to glow/binary.
   - If a subject doesn't read, set `"style":"dots"` or tweak `cell`/`gain` for that scene in scenes.json. If the wrong thing spins or the zoom target is off, set `motion`, `spin_circle` or `focus`.
7. **Send** the best preview still first, naming the chosen style.
8. **Render** the full video (same command without `--stills-only`; ~2x the song length on CPU). Then make the X copy: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 20 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart video_x.mp4`. Send both MP4s (re-encode at a lower bitrate if a file is too large to attach).

## Revisions (loop until happy)
- **Change the whole look:** pick a new style line, regenerate the images, re-render.
- **Swap an image:** rewrite that prompt, regenerate `scene_NN.png`, re-render.
- **Look per scene:** `"style"` = glow | color | dots | binary; `"cell"` (smaller = more detail); `"gain"` (brighter).
- **Motion:** `"motion"` = spin | zoom | pan; `"focus":[x,y]` (0-1) for the zoom target; `"spin_circle":[cx,cy,r]`; `"spin_zoom"` to push in.
- **Timing:** edit scene `start` values or re-run plan_scenes with a different `--target`.
- **Toggles:** drop `--lyrics-overlay` or `--skyline`.
- Always preview with `--stills-only` before a full re-render. Never post anywhere for the user; just hand over the files.

skills.name: ascii-music-video-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the ASCII music video bot.
skills.content:
---
name: ascii-music-video-getting-started
description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the ASCII music video bot.
---
Start with one line: "I turn your song into a beat-synced ASCII-art music video, with scenes drawn from your lyrics, a look picked to fit your song, and everything cut to the beat."

Then ask, one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. "Upload the song as an MP3. From Suno, open the song, use the ... menu, then Download, then MP3 Audio. Share links won't download."
2. "Got lyrics? Paste them, upload a .txt, or send the Suno song link. Or say 'transcribe' and I'll pull them from the audio."
3. "Want a particular look, like neon noir, retro arcade or woodcut ink? Or should I pick one that fits the song?"

If they named a look, save it as a profile memory as their preferred style. Then run the ascii-music-video skill. Keep the user posted (setting up, planning scenes, making images, here's a preview frame and the style I chose). Send the preview still before the full render, then deliver the MP4 plus an X-ready copy and offer revisions.
